title: Spatially-resolved relation between [C I] <SUP>3</SUP>P<SUB>1</SUB>-<SUP>3</SUP>P<SUB>0</SUB> and <SUP>12</SUP>CO (1-0) in Arp 220
question: Investigate the spatially-resolved relationship between [C I] (1-0) and CO (1-0) at ~100 pc scale in Arp 220, its dependence on the CO (3-2)/CO (1-0) ratio, and the properties of high-velocity outflow components.

data.arrays: 12 m array (35 antennas available after calibration for [C I])
data.sensitivity: [C I] (1-0): 6.3 mJy beam^-1; CO (1-0): 0.70 mJy beam^-1; CO (3-2): 1.42 mJy beam^-1 (all per 5 km s^-1 channel)

what.value: JCMT integrated [C I] (1-0) line flux density of Arp 220 (1160 +/- 350 Jy km s^-1)

evidence.quote: For example, we compare the integrated [C ] (1–0) line flux density with the measurement taken by the JCMT (1160 $\pm$ 350 Jy km s$^{-1}$ ($\Omega_{\rm PB}$ = 10$''$); (cite: Papadopoulos2004a)).

what.value: Average [C I]/CO luminosity ratio (0.22 +/- 0.09) of 20 U/LIRGs and unresolved U/LIRG luminosities

evidence.quote: The derived luminosity ratio is 0.22 $\pm$ 0.04, which is comparable to the average [C ]/CO ratio (0.22 $\pm$ 0.09) of 20 U/LIRGs presented in (cite: Valentino2018).
which is comparable to the average \[C \]/CO ratio (0.22 $\pm$ 0.09) of 20 U/LIRGs presented in (cite: Valentino2018)

what.value: [C I] (1-0) and CO (1-0) luminosities and linear relations of local galaxies (non-U/LIRGs) and average X_CI in local U/LIRGs

evidence.quote: (cite: Jiao2019) suggest that $X_{\rm CI}$ in local U/LIRGs (Avg. $X_{\rm CI} = (8.3 \pm 3.0) \times 10^{-5}$) is about three times higher than $X_{\rm CI}$ of spiral galaxies.

evidence.loc: The relation between [C I] and CO
evidence.quote: We plot the \[C \] (1-0) and CO (1–0) luminosities of Arp 220 and the literature samples of local galaxies (non-U/LIRGs) (cite: Jiao2019)

what.value: [C I] (1-0) and CO (1-0) luminosities of proto-cluster galaxies at z = 2.2

evidence.loc: The relation between [C I] and CO
evidence.quote: and proto-cluster galaxies at $z$ = 2.2 (cite: Emonts2018)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate, uv-clip, and image the archival ALMA visibilities
recipe.method: Restore calibrated MS using observatory scripts, add flagging, image line-free continuum, perform phase-only self-calibration and apply to all data, subtract continuum, clip CO (1-0) and CO (3-2) visibilities to shortest uv distance >= 26.9 klambda to match [C I] (1-0), and image cubes with 5 km s^-1 velocity resolution using Briggs robust = 0.5.
key_parameters: robust = 0.5, velocity resolution = 5 km s^-1, shortest uv distance = 26.9 klambda

recipe.goal: Create moment maps and measure kinematics
recipe.method: Create integrated intensity maps without clipping intensities, and velocity field and velocity dispersion maps after clipping cleaned image cubes at the 4sigma level per channel.
key_parameters: 4sigma per channel clipping for moment 1 and 2 maps; no clipping for moment 0

recipe.goal: Measure integrated line fluxes, luminosities, and molecular gas masses for central 5'' and high-velocity components
recipe.method: Measure integrated fluxes within the central 5'' region (radius 2.5'') and within 0.8'' x 1.0'' ellipses around high-velocity outflow peaks (-510 to -370 km s^-1 and 270 to 540 km s^-1 relative to v_sys = 5355 km s^-1), then compute L'_line and M(H2) from [C I] and CO (1-0).
key_parameters: Central aperture radius = 2.5''; outflow aperture = 0.8'' x 1.0''; blueshifted velocity range = -510 to -370 km s^-1; redshifted velocity range = 270 to 540 km s^-1
assumptions: Optically thin [C I] (1-0), D_L = 81 Mpc, A_10 = 7.93 x 10^-8 s^-1, Q_10 = 0.48 (central) or 0.47 (outflow), X_CI = 3 x 10^-5 or 8.3 x 10^-5 or 7.5 x 10^-5, alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1

recipe.goal: Fit spatially-resolved pixel-by-pixel [C I] (1-0) vs CO (1-0) luminosity relation
recipe.method: Smooth channel maps to beam-matched 0.3'' resolution, bin pixels to 57 pc x 57 pc (5 km s^-1 channels), exclude pixels < 3sigma, within 300 pc of each nucleus, or with log L'_[CI](1-0) < 5.3, and fit linear relation in log-log space using linmix.
key_parameters: beam = 0.3'', pixel size = 57 pc x 57 pc, dv = 5 km s^-1, SNR > 3sigma, r > 300 pc from nuclei, log L'_[CI](1-0) >= 5.3

recipe.goal: Analyze dependence of [C I]/CO ratio on CO (3-2)/CO (1-0) ratio (R_CO) using non-LTE RADEX radiative transfer models
recipe.method: Use CO (3-2) data in 4845-5630 km s^-1, bin pixels by R_CO (delta R_CO = 0.2 and two groups R_CO >= 1 and R_CO < 1), and compare average L'_[CI](1-0)/L'_CO(1-0) and R_CO against non-LTE RADEX radiative transfer calculations varying N_CI, T_k, and n_H2.
assumptions: Typical Galactic molecular cloud line width dV = 5 km s^-1; constant CO column density N_CO = 5 x 10^17 cm^-2 across the observed region

score_reason: All three ALMA datasets are public archival projects with clearly stated CASA versions, spectral/velocity resolutions, uv-clipping thresholds, beam sizes, and analysis packages (linmix, RADEX) and equations; however, custom flagging commands, self-calibration/cleaning details, exact aperture coordinates, and the bodies of Tables 1 and 2 are omitted.
